profile.name: Marco Jansen
profile.writeup:
With his imposing height of 2.06 meters (6.8 feet), slender frame, and large hands, Marco Jansen embodies the quintessential fast bowler's physique. Interestingly, despite his natural fit as a fast bowler, Jansen's cricketing roots lie in batting. As a young prodigy, he started his career as an opening batter and demonstrated his batting prowess early on, scoring an impressive 164 at just nine years of age. His cricketing development was nurtured by his father, who also coached Marco's younger brother Duan – a striking doppelganger who shares his brother's exceptional talents.


Marco Jansen's professional cricket journey began to take shape in April 2018, when he made his List A debut for North West in the CSA Provincial One-Day Challenge. Just months later, in October, he marked his first-class cricket debut in the CSA 3-Day Provincial Cup, where he would soon make his presence felt.


The young paceman's talent didn't go unnoticed, and in early 2019, he earned his place in South Africa's under-19 squad for their tour to India – a significant milestone in any young cricketer's career. His performances in domestic cricket were particularly impressive, as he emerged as North West's leading wicket-taker in the 2018-19 CSA 3-Day Provincial Cup, claiming 27 wickets in just six matches.


Continuing his rapid rise through South African cricket's ranks, Jansen expanded his repertoire to the shortest format of the game, making his Twenty20 debut for the Knights in April 2019. His growing reputation in domestic cricket led to another exciting opportunity when he was selected for the Durban Heat squad in the prestigious Mzansi Super League later that year.


2021 proved to be a transformative year in Marco Jansen's career. His talent caught the eye of the Mumbai franchise in the Indian T20 League. He made an immediate impact, claiming the prized wicket of the explosive Glenn Maxwell as his first dismissal in the tournament. The same year marked Jansen's entry into international cricket. While he initially received a call-up to South Africa's Test squad for their series against Pakistan, his Test debut would have to wait. The defining moment finally arrived in December 2021, when he earned his first Test cap to don the Proteas whites during South Africa's tour of India.


It didn’t take long for Marco to be South Africa’s perennial player across three formats due to his consistent performances. His journey in international cricket expanded in 2022 when he made his ODI debut against India, and shortly after, the Hyderabad franchise in the Indian T20 League recognized his potential and secured his services.


Since then, Jansen has established himself as an indispensable member of the Proteas setup, featuring prominently in major ICC tournaments in the subsequent years. What sets him apart is not just his primary skill as a fast bowler, but his valuable contributions with the bat in the lower middle order, making him a genuine all-round asset for the team.


Beyond international cricket, Jansen has made significant waves in franchise cricket worldwide. His association with the Sunrisers Eastern Cape in SA20 has been particularly successful, contributing meaningfully to their back-to-back title victories. In the third season, he had another stellar campaign winning the MVP but finished as runners-up. Jansen also played for Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL and he helped them to reach the final in 2024.


Since the 2024 T20 World Cup, Jansen has been at the heart of South Africa’s most historic achievements. In November 2024, he tore through Sri Lanka with career-best figures of 7/13, skittling them for 42 (their lowest Test score). He became the first Proteas left-arm seame to take a 10-wicket match haul at Kingsmead. All these performances compelled the selectors to include him in the Champions Trophy squad in 2025.


Jansen was a cornerstone of the Proteas side that clinched the 2023–2025 ICC World Test Championship, marking South Africa's second-ever ICC trophy. Later in Novemeber 2025, in a historic 2–0 series sweep against India, Jansen earned Player of the Match honors in the second Test. He smashed 93 (91) and took 6/48, handing India their largest-ever Test defeat (408 runs) and securing South Africa’s first series win in India in 25 years.


Marco Jansen has transitioned from a ‘talented prospect’ to one of the most feared multi-format all-rounders on the planet. Standing at 2.06m (6 ft 8 inches), he has utilized his height to become a tactical nightmare for top-order batters while evolving into a reliable lower-order finisher and will be looking to make a mark for Punjab Kings in the 2026 Indian Premier League season.
